60149017.s: Al Afnan Historic Palace in Al Sabaan Governorate is one of the old archaeological landmarks of the Hail region. It reflects the region's traditional architecture, and its mud walls evoke stories from Hail's long history.

60149006.s: New Fayd Museum is near the archaeological city of Fayd in the Hail region. It holds a collection of artefacts found around the historic city, which was a major station in the middle of the Zubaydah Trail, the pilgrimage route between Kufa and Makkah.
60149006.b: New Fayd Museum is near the archaeological city of Fayd in the Hail region. It holds a collection of artefacts found around the historic city, which was a major station in the middle of the Zubaydah Trail, the pilgrimage route between Kufa and Makkah.

60149004.s: Fayd is a historic city in the southeast of the Hail region and one of its important archaeological sites. Its mountains hold historic inscriptions dating to prehistoric times, and it was a major station on the Zubaydah Trail, halfway between Makkah and Baghdad. It was registered among the provinces of the Abbasid Caliphate and is rich in Islamic remains. Fayd is 92 km from Hail on the highway linking Hail with Al-Qassim, and 160 km from Al-Qassim.
60149004.b: Fayd is a historic city in the southeast of the Hail region and one of its important archaeological sites. Its mountains hold historic inscriptions dating to prehistoric times, and it was a major station on the Zubaydah Trail, halfway between Makkah and Baghdad. It was registered among the provinces of the Abbasid Caliphate and is rich in Islamic remains, with historical importance and standing. Fayd is 92 km from Hail on the highway linking Hail with Al-Qassim, and 160 km from Al-Qassim. Its main remains include Kharash Palace, the Zubaydah pools, the residential town, the underground passages, the hills area, the palace cistern, a giant grain-grinding millstone, about 45 wells and water channels. The city dates to the early Islamic period. It was recently announced that Fayd Historic City will be developed for tourism.

60148988.t: Rat and Al Manjor Rock Art
60148988.s: Rat and Al Manjor are two archaeological sites about 320 km south of Hail and about 35 km west of the village of Al Shuwaymis, part of Al Hait. They are among the new discoveries in Hail's archaeology, as international experts concluded after extensive analytical study of the drawings found at Al Shuwaymis, which may date back 14,000 years.

60148937.s: Fadak is an ancient historic oasis in Al Hait Governorate, about 250 kilometres southwest of Hail. It was long an important farming oasis thanks to its abundant water and fertile soil, and was known for growing dates and grain. Its springs and palm trees still bear witness to this.
60148937.b:
Fadak is an ancient historic oasis in Al Hait Governorate, about 250 kilometres southwest of Hail. It was long an important farming oasis thanks to its abundant water and fertile soil, and was known for growing dates and grain. Its springs and palm trees still bear witness to this.

Fadak saw notable historical events. The Babylonian king Nabonidus reached it on his campaign in northwest Arabia in the 6th century BC, and inscriptions attributed to him were found there. In the time of the Prophet, its people made peace with the Muslims after the conquest of Khaybar. The area has old castles and forts built of black volcanic stone, as well as Thamudic and early Islamic inscriptions.

60148934.s: Al Hait Traditional Market in Al Hait Governorate is a traditional souq that reflects the region's heritage character, with shops selling local products and handicrafts.
60148934.b: Al Hait Traditional Market in Al Hait Governorate is a traditional souq that reflects the region's heritage character, with shops selling local products and handicrafts. It is a popular destination for those who enjoy traditional shopping and learning about the customs of the local people.

60148890.s: Al Dowaili Museum is one of the museums of the Hail region. It was founded by Musab Hamid Al Ghufaili Al Shammari. The museum is in a modern two-storey building with a total area of 500 square metres, including a hall for rare and valuable pieces and several sections with domed ceilings, under which all the collection is displayed.

60148888.t: Aja and Salma Cafe and Museum
60148888.s: Aja and Salma Heritage Museum is one of the museums of the Hail region. It was founded by Fahd Al Mohammed Al Toub and sits in an area its owner set aside for social activities in Hail. The museum covers 4,500 square metres.
60148888.b: Aja and Salma Heritage Museum is one of the museums of the Hail region. It was founded by Fahd Al Mohammed Al Toub and sits in an area its owner set aside for social activities in Hail. The museum covers 4,500 square metres and consists of a main hall of 480 square metres, holding many old weapons once used in war, old coins, and large quantities of utensils used in Arab hospitality. There is also a heritage building with a series of rooms built in the old architectural style of the Hail region, displaying leatherwork, wooden doors, watering and travel equipment, clothing, woollens, a model of a traditional Al Mussakhan house with its furnishings and a family sitting room, along with a collection of old cars.

60148885.s: Al Turathi Restaurant in central Hail is an experience that combines a restaurant and a museum in an old mud building, serving traditional Hail dishes and displaying a variety of heritage items.
60148885.b:
Al Turathi Restaurant in central Hail is an experience that combines a restaurant and a museum. It was founded by Eid Al Harbi in an old mud building more than a hundred years old, with a tamarisk-wood roof. The building has two floors with about 35 rooms over roughly 1,200 square metres, and rooftop seating overlooking Hail's landmarks.

The restaurant serves traditional Hail dishes, and visitors wander through its mud rooms, which display a variety of heritage items including weapons, household vessels, coffee pots, old teapots, jewellery and carpets.

60148837.s: Al Qishlah Palace is a historic palace built in Hail during the reign of King Abdulaziz Al Saud in 1360 AH (1941). Construction took a year and a half, after which a mosque, a prison building and other annexes were added, finished in 1362 AH. The palace was built in the Najdi school of architecture, but its plaster decoration is a feature of Hail's traditional architecture, with geometric and floral motifs. The building covers 19,932 square metres, and some of the decorations include inscriptions such as "Long live our master, the great King Abdulaziz bin Abdul Rahman Al Saud."

60148834.s: Laqeet Lilmadi Athar Museum is a heritage museum in Hail, in the Labdah district close to the historic Aarif Fort.
60148834.b: Laqeet Lilmadi Athar Museum is a heritage museum in Hail, in the Labdah district close to the historic Aarif Fort. It displays a collection of old items that tell of everyday life in the Hail region in the past, and is visited by heritage enthusiasts and visitors who want to learn about the region's history.

60148832.s: Aarif Fort is an old fortress in the Hail region in the north of Saudi Arabia. The historic fort stands in the heart of Hail on top of a mountain overlooking the city, from which it takes its name. It is believed to have been built in 1840 and is one of Hail's heritage landmarks, with a position that makes it easy to see from all parts of the city.
60148832.b: Aarif Fort is an old fortress in the Hail region in the north of Saudi Arabia. The historic fort stands in the heart of Hail on top of a mountain overlooking the city, from which it takes its name. 60148830.s: Hail Regional Museum is a tourist and recreational museum owned by the Saudi Museums Commission. It is one of the most important museums in Hail and attracts many visitors, having been built to raise awareness and educate the community.
60148830.b:
Hail Regional Museum is a tourist and recreational museum owned by the Saudi Museums Commission. It is one of the most important museums in Hail and attracts many visitors, having been built to raise awareness and educate the community.

The museum tells visitors the history of a period in the Arabian Peninsula in general, and of the "Bride of the North" in particular, from prehistoric times through the beginnings of Islam to the present day, which has made it one of the region's most important cultural projects. It stands in Hail next to the Prince Sultan Cultural Centre, on a total area of about 11,000 square metres, and opened in 2004 after renovation. The museum has a unique design inspired by Hail's architecture, and is a very important addition to the region's cultural and artistic scene, with archaeological treasures, heritage items and old manuscripts that give visitors a real chance to move between eras and learn about the cultural heritage of Saudi Arabia.

60148826.s: Tawaran Palace lies 65 km northwest of Hail, in the historic and ecologically rich Wadi Tawaran in the Aja mountains. Visitors can see the remains of Tawaran Palace, the only surviving trace of the ancient village of Tawaran. The palace is one of the most important cultural sites because its name is linked to the story of Hatim Al Tai and to the Tayyi tribe that lived there. Visitors can also see the tomb of Hatim Al Tai and the tomb of his daughter, who is believed to have lived into the Islamic era, beside the palace, and the spot of the fire that Hatim Al Tai used to light at night to guide guests to his home so he could host and honour them.

60148820.s: Harrat Bani Rashid is part of Harrat Khaybar, in the southwest of the Hail region near its border with the Madinah region. It is a vast volcanic field of about 14,000 square kilometres, formed by eruptions over millions of years and covered in lava and black volcanic rock.
60148820.b:
Harrat Bani Rashid is part of Harrat Khaybar, in the southwest of the Hail region near its border with the Madinah region. It is a vast volcanic field of about 14,000 square kilometres, formed by eruptions over millions of years and covered in lava and black volcanic rock.

The harrat is known for its rare volcanoes, most notably Jabal Al Abyad (Al Bayda), distinguished by its rare white rock and a wide crater about 1,500 metres across, and beside it Jabal Al Qadr with its dark basaltic lava. This is why the site is known as the Black and White Volcanoes, and it is a destination for adventure, geology and photography enthusiasts.

60148817.s: Abu Al Hol Mountain (the Sphinx) is a unique natural rock formation in the village of Aba Al Hiran in the Aja mountain range, west of Hail. Erosion and weathering over time have carved it until it resembles a human head, which is why it is named after the famous statue in Egypt.
60148817.b:
Abu Al Hol Mountain (the Sphinx) is a unique natural rock formation in the village of Aba Al Hiran in the Aja mountain range, west of Hail. Erosion and weathering over time have carved it until it resembles a human head, which is why it is named after the famous statue in Egypt.

The mountain is a striking natural landmark in the Hail region, visited by sightseers and photography enthusiasts who come to enjoy the varied rock formations found throughout the Aja mountains.

60148815.s: Aja and Salma, or the Tayyi mountains, are the signature landmark of the Hail region. The Aja range lies to the northwest of the city and the Salma range to the southeast. Aja is the larger of the two, and the Al Butayn plain separates them.
60148815.b:
Aja and Salma, or the Tayyi mountains, are the signature landmark of the Hail region. The Aja range lies to the northwest of the city and the Salma range to the southeast. Aja is the larger of the two, and the Al Butayn plain separates them.

The mountains get their names from an ancient legend. Aja was a man from one of the Amalek tribes that lived in that part of the Arabian Peninsula, and Salma was a girl he loved, who loved him to the point of madness, but their families refused to let them marry because of certain tribal customs. One day Salma ran away with Aja, together with her maid Al Awja. Their people pursued them and caught them between the mountains of Aja and Salma, where they killed them and crucified them, Aja on the western mountain and Salma on the eastern one, and the mountains have borne their names ever since.

60148811.s: Mishar National Park in Hail offers wide green spaces and recreational facilities suited to families. It is a popular place to enjoy nature away from the bustle of the city.
60148811.b: Mishar National Park in Hail offers wide green spaces and recreational facilities suited to families. It is a popular place to spend quiet time and enjoy nature away from the bustle of the city.

60148751.s: Al Mughwah Events Park in Hail is a venue for holding events and celebrations, with large spaces for family and group occasions.
60148751.b: Al Mughwah Events Park in Hail is a venue set aside for holding various events and celebrations, with large spaces that allow family and group occasions to be organised.

60148749.s: Aja Park in Hail has many facilities to suit every member of the family, including chalets, the largest open-air amusement park in Hail, places to ride and learn to ride horses, and a shopping area with restaurants and cafés to suit your taste.
60148749.b:
Aja Park in Hail has many facilities to suit every member of the family, including chalets, the largest open-air amusement park in Hail, places to ride and learn to ride horses, and a shopping area with restaurants and cafés to suit your taste.

On entering Aja Park you are greeted by a shopping area from which to start your visit. Inside is a large amusement park with many electric and air-powered rides, and as you rise high on them you can see Hail's towering mountains.

The park also has a theatre for events, as well as cottages, camps and chalets for rent with a variety of unique seating styles and sizes. These include seating in the Greek style, with its calming dominant blue, chalets in a rustic design, chalets in a traditional style, and simple floor seating that feels relaxed and comfortable.

Aja Park welcomes all visitors daily from 1:30 pm to 2:00 am in summer, and from 3:00 pm to 1:00 am in winter.

60148746.s: Hail Boulevard is a modern entertainment destination that brings together restaurants, cafés and shops in a contemporary atmosphere, where locals and visitors spend their evenings in Hail.
60148746.b: Hail Boulevard is a modern entertainment destination that brings together restaurants, cafés and shops in a bright, contemporary atmosphere. It is one of the main places locals and visitors go to spend their evenings in Hail.

60148743.s: Al Samra Park is a magical sunset spot with a variety of cafés and restaurants and a superb view over Hail. It stands on Mount Al Samra, whose name is linked to Hatim Al Tai, the symbol of generosity, who is said to have lit a fire on the mountain to guide travellers to his home.
60148743.b:
Al Samra Park is a magical sunset spot with a variety of cafés and restaurants and a superb view over Hail. It stands on Mount Al Samra, whose name is linked to Hatim Al Tai, the symbol of generosity, who is said to have lit a fire on the mountain to guide travellers to his home.

The entry fee for a car is roughly 20 to 25 riyals.

60148433.s: The ruins and stone towers sit on top of a rocky plateau near the town of Al Quwarah in the Al-Qassim region. The site is linked to the story of the pre-Islamic poet Antarah ibn Shaddad, and Thamudic inscriptions and rock drawings have been found around it.
60148433.b: The ruins of Antarah Palace sit on top of a rocky plateau known as Jaal Qusaiba, near the town of Al Quwarah in the Al-Qassim region. They include ruins and stone towers believed to have been used for guarding and for watching over the springs and palm orchards. The site is linked to the story of the pre-Islamic poet Antarah ibn Shaddad, and Thamudic inscriptions and rock drawings depicting ibex and camels have been found around it.

60148369.s: Mashqouq Palace, also known as Al Radi Palace, is in the centre of Qusaiba north of Buraydah, and its construction began in 1250 AH.
60148369.b: Mashqouq Palace, also known as Al Radi Palace, is in the centre of Qusaiba north of Buraydah, and its construction began in 1250 AH. The palace is built of mud and stone, with a roof of tamarisk wood and palm fronds. Its walls are about 15 metres high and it is surrounded by a wall, with majlis rooms, a mosque and other rooms. It is called Mashqouq ("split") because it was built over the course of a spring whose channel was cut underground to bring water to the palace's well.

60148366.s: Al Khabra Old Town was built more than 200 years ago from pure clay, which made it strong against time and erosion. It has more than 400 houses, built in a circular form resembling the layout of Baghdad in the Abbasid era, and has stayed intact. The village surrounds the Majlis souq and the mosque in a circle, so places of buying and selling lie in the middle of the town. The old town is in the middle of the Al-Qassim region of Saudi Arabia, on an area of 120,000 square metres, and was built around 1115 AH. It has been described as a sturdy fortress that stood up to invasions and military campaigns.
60148366.b: Al Khabra Old Town was built more than 200 years ago from pure clay, which made it strong against time and erosion. It has more than 400 houses, built in a circular form resembling the layout of Baghdad in the Abbasid era, and has stayed intact. The village surrounds the Majlis souq and the mosque in a circle, so places of buying and selling lie in the middle of the town. The old town is in the middle of the Al-Qassim region of Saudi Arabia, on an area of 120,000 square metres, and was built around 1115 AH. It has been described as a sturdy fortress that stood up to invasions and military campaigns. It is called Al Khabra because it was a place where rainwater and overflow from Wadi Al Rumah, the largest valley in the Arabian Peninsula, once collected. It was also called Khabra Al Afalik after the Al Afalik family, its first inhabitants in the first millennium AH.
